newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish military says search launched for pilot.
newsitem.headline: Turkish military says search launched for pilot.

text.p: The Turkish military said on Tuesday a search had been launched for one of the two pilots of a Turkish F-16 fighter plane that crashed after being intercepted by Greek warplanes near the eastern Aegean island of Chios.
"Air and sea search and rescue operations are continuing for flight lieutenant Nail Erdogan," Turkish military headquarters said in a statement.
The statement said the crash, during a routine training flight, was being investigated.
The plane's other pilot Osman Cicekli, who was taken to hospital in Chios after being rescued by a Greek helicopter, was in good health, the statement said.

Greek Defence Ministry officials earlier said the pilot had radioed he was abandoning the plane after being intercepted by two Greek Mirage 2000s. No shots were fired during the interception, they added.
Greece has initiated diplomatic procedures to hand him over to Turkish authorities, the officials said.

The incident occurred on the last day of joint Greek-Cypriot military exercises -- "Nikiforos" on Cyprus and "Toxotis" in the southern Aegean. The exercises stem from a 1993 military pact between Greece and the Cypriot government, which controls the southern, Greek-populated part of the divided island.
Turkish troops occupy the northern thrid of the island.

Greece reported more than 50 airspace violations since Monday, when the exercises started. Greek fighter planes were scrambled more than 40 times to intercept Turkish planes on Monday alone, the officials said.
